lineage_context.teaching_goal: Use opposite exstipulate leaves, fused contorted corolla and superior many-ovuled capsule to orient within Gentianales, then contrast stipules, ovary position and latex.

project_scope.selection_mode: Central Texas family-first module with Zeltnera/Centaurium, Eustoma and Sabatia doors
project_scope.note: Source pool contains several historical/synonym concepts. Current-name reconciliation is taught explicitly instead of creating duplicate genus/species lessons.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: Start at a node: leaves are commonly opposite, simple, entire and without stipules. Then inspect the flower for a fused 4–5-part corolla with stamens attached to the tube and alternating with the lobes; confirm a superior ovary with many ovules and a many-seeded capsule.
family_diagnostics.vegetative: Mostly herbs in the local pool, often glabrous. Leaves commonly opposite and entire; stipules absent.
family_diagnostics.reproductive: Flowers usually bisexual and radial, commonly 4- or 5-merous. Corolla lobes are fused and often contorted in bud. Stamens equal the corolla lobes and alternate with them. Ovary superior, usually 2-carpellate and 1-locular with two parietal placentae.
family_diagnostics.fruit: Usually a many-seeded capsule, commonly opening by two valves.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: Opposite leaves alone are not enough. Opposite + no stipules + fused flower + superior many-seeded capsule is the useful family package.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: opposite exstipulate node → fused corolla → superior ovary/capsule → genus doors → Gentianales comparison
visual_lesson.intro: Gentianaceae looks familiar because several Gentianales families use opposite leaves and fused flowers. The trick is the missing stipules, superior ovary and many-seeded capsule.

steps.title: 1 · Check the node for missing stipules
steps.look_for: Pairs of simple entire leaves with no interpetiolar stipule or stipular line.
steps.why_it_matters: This is a fast split from Rubiaceae and many Loganiaceae.

steps.title: 2 · Read the fused, usually contorted corolla
steps.look_for: A tubular/funnelform/rotate corolla with 4–5 fused lobes; lobes often overlap in a twisted/contorted pattern in bud.
steps.why_it_matters: Connects the family to Gentianales while giving a repeatable floral clue.

steps.title: 3 · Follow the superior ovary into a capsule
steps.look_for: Ovary sits above the other floral whorls and contains many ovules; fruit commonly opens as a many-seeded capsule.
steps.why_it_matters: Separates the family from Rubiaceae's inferior ovary and from fleshy-fruited lookalikes.

steps.title: 4 · Zeltnera/Centaurium door: small pink centauries
steps.look_for: Small slender herbs with pink 5-merous flowers. Use current accepted genus rather than assuming every old Centaurium source row stays Centaurium.
steps.why_it_matters: Modern North American centaury taxonomy is one of the project's main duplicate-name traps.

steps.title: 5 · Eustoma door: the large-flowered gentian
steps.look_for: Large showy blue-purple/pink/white fused flowers on glaucous herbs; fruit remains a gentian-type capsule.
steps.why_it_matters: Shows how different family members can look while retaining the same reproductive plan.

steps.title: 6 · Sabatia door: starry flower + deeply divided stigma
steps.look_for: Star-like pink flower and a style/stigma that can be deeply divided; family fruit remains capsular.
steps.why_it_matters: Gives a third visual doorway without reducing gentians to blue tubular flowers.

comparisons.title: Gentianaceae vs Rubiaceae
comparisons.rule: Both often have opposite leaves and fused flowers. Gentianaceae is generally exstipulate with a superior ovary; Rubiaceae has interpetiolar stipules and an inferior ovary.

comparisons.title: Gentianaceae vs Apocynaceae
comparisons.rule: Both often have opposite leaves and fused contorted corollas. Apocynaceae commonly has milky latex and a paired-carpel fruit/gynoecium pattern; Gentianaceae lacks the latex clue and commonly has one superior many-ovuled ovary producing a capsule.

comparisons.title: Gentianaceae vs Loganiaceae
comparisons.rule: Gentianaceae is exstipulate and commonly has a 1-locular ovary with parietal placentation; Loganiaceae may show stipules/interpetiolar lines and commonly has a 2-locular axile ovary.

visual_lesson.caveat: Gentianaceae is diverse; opposite leaves, 5-merous flowers and capsules all have exceptions. Use the node + ovary/fruit + corolla suite.
